column3: I'll send the deck Friday. Can you intro me to Sara? Most promises are spoken, and most of them are never written down.
An AI listening to a conversation can invent a promise. In DEXTRA the AI only proposes. If the words aren't in what was actually said, it never reaches your glasses.
DEXTRA runs on Even G2. It keeps the last forty-five seconds in phone memory only. Agreed something? Hold the temple, and the lens shows who promised what, each line backed by their words.
One tap sends it as you, into the Telegram chat you already have with them. No new app for them to install.
Nothing counts until they confirm. Then you both hold the same record, sealed with a fingerprint of exactly what was agreed.
You both tick items off. Whoever owes something gets a reminder the day before, on the day, and if it slips.
A hundred and twelve tests pass. On twelve labelled conversations, precision is one point oh, recall point nine four, and no invented promise got through.
DEXTRA. Said, and done. Try it with two Telegram accounts, no glasses needed.
